title: Improve weather UX with geolocation, WMO mapping, scene states, and unit coverage
body:
This updates the app from a static NYC-only demo into a weather-aware experience: current conditions are now human-readable, location-aware, and reflected in the 3D scene. It also rounds out the data model and adds unit coverage for the new parsing/mapping logic. - **Weather presentation** - Replaced raw WMO code output with a shared `wmoCode` utility that maps standard WMO codes to descriptions and emojis. - Expanded the card to show wind speed and humidity. - Replaced the loading text with a Tailwind skeleton state. - Added retry support for error states via `onRetry`. - **Location handling** - `App.tsx` now resolves coordinates from `navigator.geolocation.getCurrentPosition()`. - Falls back to the existing NYC coordinates when geolocation is unavailable or denied. - Surfaces the active location in the card. - **3D scene behavior** - `WeatherScene` now accepts `weatherCode: number | null`. - Scene background, cloud density, opacity, and tone now vary by weather group: - clear - partly cloudy - fog - rain - snow - thunderstorm - Split the `OrbitControls` props across lines for readability. - **API and typing cleanup** - Extracted the Open-Meteo response shape into a named `OpenMeteoResponse` interface. - Extended `fetchCurrentWeather` to request and return: - `wind_speed_10m` - `relative_humidity_2m` - **Project cleanup** - Removed dead `src/App.css` Vite scaffold CSS. - Updated `index.html` metadata: - title → `Interactive Weather App` - added a basic description meta tag - **Unit tests** - Added Vitest and a `test` script. - Added focused tests for: - WMO code mapping fallback and known values - weather API happy path - non-OK responses - missing required response fields Example of the shared WMO mapping API: ```ts import { getWmoCodeInfo } from './utils/wmoCode' const weather = getWmoCodeInfo(61) // { description: 'Slight Rain', emoji: '🌧️' } ```
Original prompt Implement all of the following improvements to the interactive weather app. These are grouped by priority: --- ## 🔴 Critical ### 1. Delete dead `App.css` The entire `src/App.css` file contains leftover Vite scaffold boilerplate (`.counter`, `.hero`, `#next-steps`, etc.) — none of these classes are used anywhere in the app. The project uses Tailwind exclusively. Delete `src/App.css` and remove any import of it (check `src/main.tsx` and `src/App.tsx`). ### 2. Add WMO code → human-readable description map `WeatherCard` currently shows raw `WMO Code: 61` which is meaningless to users. Create a utility (e.g. `src/utils/wmoCode.ts`) that maps WMO weather codes to: - A human-readable description (e.g. `61 → "Slight Rain"`, `0 → "Clear Sky"`) - A weather emoji (e.g. `0 → "☀️"`, `61 → "🌧️"`) Use the standard WMO code table covering at minimum: 0, 1, 2, 3, 45, 48, 51, 53, 55, 61, 63, 65, 71, 73, 75, 80, 81, 82, 95, 96, 99. Update `WeatherCard` to display the description and emoji instead of the raw WMO code number. ### 3. Use `navigator.geolocation` to get user's location In `App.tsx`, attempt to get the user's real location via `navigator.geolocation.getCurrentPosition()` before fetching weather. Fall back to the hardcoded NYC coordinates (`{ latitude: 40.7128, longitude: -74.006 }`) if geolocation is denied or unavailable. Show the city/coordinates being used somewhere in the `WeatherCard` (even just lat/lon is fine). --- ## 🟡 Medium ### 4. Make `WeatherScene` weather-aware Pass `weatherCode: number | null` as a prop to `WeatherScene`. Based on the WMO code group, change the scene: - **Clear (code 0–1):** bright blue sky (`#7dd3fc`), no clouds or very few - **Partly cloudy (code 2–3):** current default (light blue + clouds) - **Fog (45, 48):** grey-white sky (`#d1d5db`), dense low clouds - **Rain (51–65, 80–82):** dark sky (`#475569`), more clouds, higher cloud opacity - **Snow (71–75):** pale sky (`#e2e8f0`), white clouds - **Thunderstorm (95–99):** very dark sky (`#1e293b`), dense clouds ### 5. Add retry button on error In `WeatherCard`, add an `onRetry?: () => void` prop. When `error` is non-null and `onRetry` is provided, render a "Try again" button below the error message. Wire this up in `App.tsx` so clicking it re-triggers the weather fetch. ### 6. Extract `OpenMeteoResponse` interface In `src/api/weather.ts`, extract the inline anonymous response type into a named `interface OpenMeteoResponse` for clarity and future extensibility. --- ## 🟢 Minor ### 7. Add wind speed and humidity to API call Extend `fetchCurrentWeather` in `src/api/weather.ts` to also fetch `wind_speed_10m` and `relative_humidity_2m` from the Open-Meteo API. Add these fields to the `WeatherData` interface. Display them in `WeatherCard` (e.g. "Wind: 12 km/h · Humidity: 65%"). ### 8. Fix `index.html` title Set the `` in `index.html` to `"Interactive Weather App"` and add a basic `<meta name="description">` tag. ### 9. Add loading skeleton animation Replace the plain `"Loading…"` text in `WeatherCard` with an animated skeleton placeholder (pulsing grey bars using Tailwind's `animate-pulse`). ### 10. Fix long `OrbitControls` line In `WeatherScene.tsx`, split the `<OrbitControls ... />` props onto multiple lines for readability. ### 11. Add `vitest` unit tests Add `vitest` as a dev dependency and create unit tests for: - `src/utils/wmoCode.ts` — test that known codes return the correct description and emoji, and that unknown codes return a sensible fallback - `src/api/weather.ts` — test `fetchCurrentWeather` by mocking `fetch`: test the happy path, a non-ok response, and missing fields in the response Create test files at `src/utils/wmoCode.test.ts` and `src/api/weather.test.ts`. Add a `"test": "vitest run"` script to `package.json`. The following is the prior conversation context from the user's chat exploration (may be truncated): User: Review the project and refactor/review it Assistant: I've reviewed the entire codebase. Here's my comprehensive review and refactoring recommendations: --- ## 📋 Code Review: `EboveR/interactive-weather-app` ### Architecture Overview This is a **React + TypeScript + Vite** app using **Three.js / React Three Fiber** for a 3D weather scene with an **Open-Meteo** API integration. The structure is clean and modern. Here's what I found across each layer: --- ### 🔴 Critical Issues #### 1. `src/App.css` is entirely dead code The entire file contains leftover Vite scaffold boilerplate (`.counter`, `.hero`, `#next-steps`, etc.) — **none of these classes are used anywhere in the app**. The project uses Tailwind exclusively. **Fix:** Delete `src/App.css` entirely (and remove its import if it exists in `main.tsx`). #### 2. `WeatherCard` displays raw WMO code — not user-friendly ```tsx name=src/components/ui/WeatherCard.tsx url=https://github.com/EboveR/interactive-weather-app/blob/main/src/components/ui/WeatherCard.tsx#L22 <p className="mt-3 text-sm text-white/80">WMO Code: {weathe... </details> <!-- START COPILOT CODING AGENT SUFFIX --> *This pull request was created from Copilot chat.* >
